standard_prerequisites.name: The Yoneda lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the object v(P) representing the prescribed functor A -> Hom_B(P, u(A)) up to unique isomorphism, which is how the functor is defined on the chosen set of objects.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quotients and exact sequences in an abelian category
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the standard description of an object as the quotient of a map onto it and the exactness of the resulting sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the author choose an exact sequence P_2 -> P_1 -> B -> 0 for an arbitrary object B, which is what extends the construction beyond the chosen set.

core_obligations: Defining the functor on the chosen objects (proof lines 7622-7644): by Yoneda the object v(P) with Hom_A(v(P), A) = Hom_B(P, u(A)) is determined up to unique isomorphism; the map i_P : P -> u(v(P)) corresponds to the identity and the bijection is given by composition with i_P; for a pair of objects the map Hom_B(P_2, P_1) -> Hom_A(v(P_2), v(P_1)) is characterized by the rule u(v(phi)) i_{P_2} = i_{P_1} phi, and it is compatible with composition, so the assignment is a functor on the full subcategory on the chosen objects.

Extending to all objects (proof lines 7646-7665): for an arbitrary object B the author chooses an exact sequence P_2 -> P_1 -> B -> 0 and defines v(B) by the exact sequence v(P_2) -> v(P_1) -> v(B) -> 0, then computes Hom_A(v(B), A) as a kernel, rewrites it through the defining property of v on the chosen objects, and identifies it with Hom_B(B, u(A)).

Conclusion (proof lines 7667-7670): the computation shows that the construction no longer depends on having chosen a proper subset, so one may take the chosen set to be all objects and v is everywhere defined.
proof_roadmap: Represent the prescribed functors by objects using Yoneda and get the functor on the chosen subcategory.
Choose a presentation of an arbitrary object by objects of the chosen set.
Define the value there by an exact sequence and compute the Hom-set to get the adjunction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a functor admitting a set of objects covering the target by quotients, on which the representing objects of the presheaves A -> Hom(P, u(A)) exist, has a left adjoint (statement lines 7604-7619). The proof is a complete argument: the representability hypothesis and Yoneda give the functor on the chosen full subcategory together with the characterising rule for its action on morphisms (proof lines 7622-7644); an arbitrary object is presented as a quotient of objects from the chosen set, the value of the functor there is defined by an exact sequence, and the Hom-set computation identifies it with the one required for the adjunction (proof lines 7646-7665); the final step observes that the chosen set may be taken to be everything (proof lines 7667-7670). The non-formal content is the Hom-set computation for an arbitrary object. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
